messages.subject: Executive Value Proposition | AD Ports Group | Government Relations, ESG & International Growth
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Hammoud,

I am writing to share a strategic value proposition prepared specifically for AD Ports Group as the Group continues to expand its international trade, logistics, ports and economic-zone platform while strengthening sustainability and stakeholder governance.

I currently serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department, at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My mandate spans senior government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, social performance, strategic partnerships, stakeholder strategy and executive advisory within a capital-intensive multinational operating environment. I work across public institutions, communities, technical teams and senior management to convert external expectations into accountable execution.

AD Ports Group's direction is strongly aligned with my experience. The Group operates across more than 50 countries, manages a growing international portfolio of terminals, logistics and economic-zone assets, and has aligned its Sustainability Strategy 2026-2030 with global standards. My background brings practical experience where government relationships, regulatory requirements, ESG evidence, stakeholder expectations and major-asset delivery meet.

Rather than send a conventional CV alone, I have attached an AD Ports Group-specific strategic value brief. It identifies areas where I believe my experience could support the Group across international stakeholder strategy, government and regulatory relations, ESG execution, country readiness, strategic partnerships and executive issues management. It also includes a 90-180 day action framework and my three-page executive CV.

Given your position at the centre of the Group's investor and external interface, I would value your perspective on where this profile may fit best. If another executive owns the most relevant mandate across Sustainability, Strategy and Growth, International Business, Corporate Affairs or Government Relations, I would appreciate your guidance or internal referral.

Kind regards,

Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director | AGM Inc., Zijin Mining Group
Georgetown, Guyana
+592 608 4735
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposition for AD Ports Group
strategic_brief.executive_summary: AD Ports Group has evolved into a global platform spanning ports, economic cities and free zones, maritime and shipping, logistics and digital services, with international growth now central to its value-creation model. That scale increases the importance of disciplined country-level execution across governments, regulators, partners, communities and portfolio businesses. My value proposition is to strengthen the institutional layer connecting strategy with external execution. As Liaison Director at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group, I lead country-facing government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, social responsibility, stakeholder strategy and executive advisory in a capital-intensive multinational operating environment. I would bring AD Ports Group practical experience in multi-agency coordination, ESG evidence, strategic partnerships, social performance and executive issue management that is relevant to international expansion, major infrastructure, economic zones and long-term stakeholder confidence.
strategic_brief.company_context: AD Ports Group's 2025 annual and sustainability reporting reflects a business that has moved well beyond a domestic port operator into a vertically integrated international trade and logistics group. The portfolio comprises dozens of terminals, operates across more than 50 countries and includes economic zones, logistics, maritime and digital capabilities. In 2025 the Group aligned its Sustainability Strategy 2026-2030 to global standards, developed decarbonisation plans for business clusters, completed more than 200 CSR initiatives and reported a 95 percent improvement in its external ESG rating over three years. Its stakeholder engagement policy places governments, regulators, customers, suppliers, investors and communities within a formal governance framework. As the international portfolio grows, disciplined government relations, stakeholder intelligence, ESG execution and country readiness become increasingly important to protecting investment outcomes and strengthening long-term operating legitimacy.

opportunities.title: International Government and Stakeholder Architecture
opportunities.rationale: AD Ports Group's international assets depend on port authorities, ministries, customs agencies, investment bodies, regulators, local partners and communities. A consistent stakeholder architecture across priority markets would give leadership clearer visibility of institutional dependencies, decision pathways, commitments and emerging issues before they affect concessions, project schedules or operating performance.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would map priority institutions, relationship ownership, approval pathways and stakeholder expectations across selected markets, then establish executive briefs, engagement plans, commitment trackers and escalation routes. My current role applies this discipline across multiple public agencies and regulated operating functions where timing, trust and follow-through directly affect business continuity.

opportunities.title: Country Readiness for International Growth
opportunities.rationale: Expansion into new markets requires more than transaction execution. Infrastructure and logistics projects bring permitting, local-content, workforce, community, environmental, political and social expectations that need to be integrated early into investment and operating plans. A common country-readiness framework would help identify these dependencies before capital, reputation and executive attention are committed.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would develop a practical readiness model combining government relations, regulatory mapping, ESG obligations, stakeholder analysis, local economic considerations and implementation ownership. My multinational mining experience involves translating global corporate requirements into country-level operating action across complex public-sector and community interfaces.

opportunities.title: ESG Evidence and Decarbonisation Governance
opportunities.rationale: AD Ports Group has established an ambitious 2026-2030 sustainability agenda across diverse business clusters and geographies. As decarbonisation and ESG initiatives scale, leadership needs consistent source evidence, named owners, review processes and clear linkage between operational performance, public commitments and external reporting across subsidiaries and assets.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support ESG governance by linking commitments to operating evidence, stakeholder expectations, accountable owners and concise executive reporting. My experience includes carbon-data traceability using physical operating records and stakeholder governance around approximately 46-50 MWp of solar capacity and more than 80 MWh of battery storage.

opportunities.title: Strategic Partnerships and Economic Development
opportunities.rationale: Ports, economic zones and logistics platforms create value through ecosystems of governments, investors, industrial tenants, contractors, communities and trade partners. The strongest partnerships align commercial objectives with national development, employment, local business participation, sustainable infrastructure and long-term competitiveness rather than treating stakeholder engagement as a separate support function.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would structure partnership and stakeholder plans that connect commercial priorities with government objectives, investment agencies, industry partners, workforce institutions and community outcomes. My current mandate combines government engagement, strategic partnerships, local economic interfaces and social performance around a major multinational mining operation.

opportunities.title: Executive Issues and Reputation Readiness
opportunities.rationale: International infrastructure operators face reputation-sensitive issues involving regulation, environmental performance, community concerns, labour, concessions and public-sector commitments. Effective executive response depends on verified facts, clear internal ownership and disciplined escalation across operations, legal, sustainability, communications and senior management before an operational issue becomes a wider institutional problem.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would establish concise executive decision briefs, stakeholder-risk registers, evidence trackers and escalation protocols for priority matters. I routinely coordinate regulator-facing and reputation-sensitive issues across operations, HSE, environment, legal, finance, procurement, HR, security, aviation and technical teams, with emphasis on accuracy, ownership and closure.

days_0_30: Confirm the markets, clusters or strategic projects where external stakeholder complexity creates the greatest execution need.
Map priority government, regulatory, community, partner and investor interfaces against live business objectives and existing relationship ownership.
Review stakeholder intelligence, commitments, ESG evidence and executive escalation processes for gaps and duplication.
days_31_60: Select three to five priority pilots based on strategic value, stakeholder complexity and leadership sponsorship.
Build integrated country and stakeholder plans with objectives, ownership, evidence requirements, milestones and escalation thresholds.
Create an executive dashboard covering institutional dependencies, regulatory milestones, commitments, emerging risks and partnership opportunities.
days_61_90: Launch pilot engagement plans with agreed executive sponsors and structured briefing materials.
Embed ESG and stakeholder evidence into selected project or market reviews.
Establish a lessons process to identify repeatable practices across clusters and geographies.
days_91_180: Scale effective practices into a common toolkit for international stakeholder strategy and country readiness.
Measure impact through decision-cycle time, commitment closure, regulatory progress, stakeholder outcomes and evidence quality.
Institutionalize leadership reporting on material external dependencies and reputation-sensitive issues across priority markets.

potential_impact: Earlier visibility of government, regulatory and stakeholder dependencies around international investments and operating assets.
Stronger country-level readiness before new capital and reputation are committed.
More consistent translation of ESG and decarbonisation commitments into operating evidence and accountable actions.
Higher-quality strategic partnerships connecting commercial objectives with national and local development priorities.
Faster executive decisions through disciplined issue governance and cross-functional accountability.
background_relevance: Current Liaison Director at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group, with country-facing responsibility spanning government and regulatory relations, ESG, social responsibility, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive communications.
Leads senior institutional engagement across mining, environment, energy, aviation, labour, standards, taxation, trade, investment and social-performance matters.

Coordinates permits, inspections, official visits, external commitments and sensitive matters across operations, HSE, environment, legal, HR, finance, procurement, security, aviation and technical teams.
Supports stakeholder governance around approximately 46-50 MWp of solar capacity and more than 80 MWh of battery storage.
Coordinated a 2026 carbon-accounting proof of concept using physical operating data to strengthen traceability and review readiness.
Brings 12+ years across multinational mining, regulated financial services and commercial operations, supported by an MBA and international executive-development exposure.
